items.actClause:
AN ACT to amend the tax law and the state finance law, in relation to
providing for taxpayer gifts for Lyme and tick-borne diseases education,
research and prevention and establishing the Lyme and tick-borne diseases
education, research and prevention fund
items.lawCode: Add §§209-N & 630-i, Tax L; add §95-j, St Fin L
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S6871

SPONSOR: HARCKHAM
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the tax law and the state finance law, in relation to
providing for taxpayer gifts for Lyme and tick-borne diseases education,
research and prevention and establishing the Lyme and tick-borne
diseases education, research and prevention fund

 
PURPOSE:

To establish a tax checkoff for Lyme and tick-borne diseases education,
research and prevention efforts.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1: Adds a new section 209-N to the Tax Law to allow for gifts
for Lyme and tick-borne diseases education, research and prevention.
Contributions shall be in the whole dollar amount and not reduce the
amount of state tax owed by the taxpayer.

Section 2: Adds a new section 630-i of the Tax Law to add similar
provisions.

Section 3: Adds a new section 95-j of the State Finance Law to establish
the Lyme and tick-borne diseases education, research and prevention
fund. Monies from the fund shall be dedicated toward Lyme and tick-borne
diseases education, research and prevention efforts approved by the
Department of Health. Provides for reporting requirements regarding the
utilization of such monies.

Section 4: Provides the effective date.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

According to the New York State Department of Health, nearly 10,000
cases of Lyme and tick-borne diseases are reported to the Department
each year. Although the Hudson Valley and Long Island have historically
been the epicenter of the Lyme epidemic in New York State, the threat
posed by ticks continues to increase and spread to portions of the state
that in prior years have seen far fewer cases. Education and prevention
efforts have made a significant impact on warning New Yorkers and visi-
tors to take necessary precautions to avoid contracting-one of these
potentially devastating illnesses, however funding to addresses this
crisis has not yet reached levels commensurate to the toll it has taken
on New Yorkers. For this reason it is essential to pursue every avail-
able avenue to ensure that critical efforts on education, prevention and
research can move forward to progress in this fight.

This legislation would allow taxpayers to voluntarily contribute toward
Lyme and TBD education, prevention and prevention efforts to help ensure
we have the resources needed to tackle this challenge.  Not only is New
York continuing to suffer the longstanding epidemic of Lyme disease, but
we are facing threats from rarer TBDs such as Powassan virus. Further-
more, new ticks, such as the Asian longhorned tick have recently been
reported as having arrived in the state, and now, more than ever, we
need to push forward and commit appropriate resources to addressing this
issue.
 
LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

2020: S8681 Referred to Rules

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

None

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect immediately and shall apply to taxable years
commencing on or after January 1, 2021.
